results.description:
Maccy is a clipboard manager doing one job - keeping your copy history at hand. Period.

• Blazing fast. Open and search your entire clipboard history in a fraction of a second. Nothing distracts you from what you're focused on.
• Keyboard-first. Just type what you want to find and hit Enter. Don't waste your time moving your hands away from the keyboard.
• Native and minimalistic design. Don't get distracted by a sophisticated interface and useless features. Feels like the operating system has a built-in clipboard manager.
• Secure and private. Password managers are not logged. All the data is stored on your Mac and never leaves it.
• Customizable and extensible. Configure every aspect in preferences. Automate complex cases with Shortcuts actions.
• Open source. The source code is available on GitHub under the MIT license. This version is being sold on the App Store to support the development.

PasteMe é um gerenciador de área de transferência para macOS, simples e focado em privacidade.

O PasteMe pode aparecer ao lado do cursor, no centro da tela ou pela barra de menus. Fixe itens importantes, remova a formatação para manter apenas texto simples, crie listas para trechos reutilizáveis e exclua apps como gerenciadores de senha quando não quiser registrar cópias.

results.description:
Folder Hub is an app hidden under the MacBook's notch, used for quick access and retrieval of files and folders within the working directory.

What problems does Folder Hub solve?

- In daily work, we often deal with numerous files and folders, typically organizing them into different directories for various projects. However, accessing specific project files often involves navigating through layers of nested folders.
- Accidentally closing a folder window means having to go through the entire folder structure again to locate the desired file.
- Even when the window is open, accessing the required files can be difficult due to other active windows, such as a web browser, obscuring the view.

How does Folder Hub address these issues (interaction design)?

The Folder Hub window is by default concealed under the MacBook's notch. When the mouse moves to the notch area, the Folder Hub window becomes visible, and upon moving the mouse out of the window, Folder Hub hides again.

When displayed, Folder Hub showcases different workspaces such as Desktop, Downloads, Project A, Project B, all of which are user-customizable and contain the respective project's files and folders. Switching between different workspaces is achieved by hovering the mouse over the respective area.

Taking image uploads as an example:
Suppose we need to upload images from "Project A" to a browser window. By moving the mouse to the notch area and then hovering over the "Project A" workspace, we can directly drag and drop the images from this workspace to the browser.

Through this simple example, the following can be observed:
- No need to navigate through nested folders
- Folder Hub floats above all other windows, ensuring it is not obscured by the current active window
- When needing to access it again, Folder Hub remains in the last selected workspace, avoiding the inconvenience of having to find the previously closed Finder window. 

- Features:
* Multi-monitor support
* Window selection for files in full-screen mode
* Drag and drop folders/files to the working directory
* Folder navigation/jump
* Custom creation of working directories
* Pin
* Preview
* Share
* Move to Trash
* Show in Finder
* Open with specified app
* Cmd + click = Show in Finder
* Control + click = AirDrop
* Copy
* Paste
* Sorting options
